name: Market Sizing
description: Estimate total market demand or opportunity.
business_contexts: private equity firm evaluating a new market entry
corporate strategy team sizing an adjacent market
venture fund screening a potential investment
question_patterns: What is the total addressable market for this product?
How large is the opportunity if the client captures its target share?
What annual revenue is available in this segment?
Is this market large enough to justify the investment?
solution_logic: Step 1: Identify addressable population = target_population × addressable_segment
Step 2: Apply penetration rate = addressable_population × penetration_rate
Step 3: Calculate annual spend per user = purchase_frequency × avg_spend_per_purchase
key_insight: Market sizing is about defensible assumptions, not precision. Show your logic clearly — the interviewer is testing your structure, not your arithmetic.
common_mistakes: Sizing the total population instead of the addressable segment
Forgetting purchase frequency — confusing annual vs per-transaction spend
Not sanity-checking the output against known benchmarks
framework_soundbite: Top-down or bottom-up — pick one, state your assumptions, and sanity-check the output. The logic matters more than the number.
